label: Aristotle, Metaphysics IV.7, 1012a9-12: No number is neither odd nor not odd
interpretation: 'In those genera in which the negation implies the contrary, there will be [intermediates] too, for example in numbers a number neither odd nor not odd; but this is impossible, as is clear from the definition.' Read as: no number is neither odd nor not odd. Not separately formalized. Note for the intuitionist comparison: parity of natural numbers is decidable, so the intuitionist grants even n odd ∨ ¬ n odd for every n; the example concerns a decidable domain and does not bear on withholding.
